superseded_calls.notes: The English adds 'belonging (as the print has it) to nature and not to grace' which is not present in the source Latin. The Latin states: 'justitiam & sanctitatem, quae in primo homine fuit, non solum fuisse donum supernaturale, & quod ad naturam non ad gratiam pertinebat;' meaning 'justice and holiness, which was in the first man, was not only a supernatural gift, and which pertains to nature and not to grace;' The English inserts '(as the print has it)' as an explanatory addition not in the source, constituting an invented addition under completeness check.

The translation mistranslated 'non solum fuisse donum supernaturale, & quod ad naturam non ad gratiam pertinebat' by stating that it belonged 'to nature and not to grace', whereas the Latin clearly says 'supernatural gift, and which pertained to grace, not to nature' (non ad naturam, sed ad gratiam / non ad naturam non ad gratiam). Furthermore, there is a clear translation error regarding the Catholic theological distinction between supernatural gifts and natural gifts.
